slides.heading: 1. Practice *for free*
paras: The Practice Interview is free, can be repeated and is never shown to companies.
The real one takes about 20 minutes.

slides.heading: 2. Pass the *setup checks*
paras: Use Chrome on a computer. A working mic is required, plus full screen sharing when asked.
Face in frame and good light make a clear recording.

slides.heading: 3. Keep answers *tight*
paras: Long silences make the AI jump in. If it cuts you off, say you were not finished.

paras: Retake from the Assessments tab. Only the latest attempt counts.
Hiring managers can see how many retakes you used.

paragraphs.text: How to pass the Mercor AI interview starts with knowing what it is. Mercor is a hiring platform that matches experts with paid projects, and its help center says every candidate is screened by an AI interviewer that asks questions about the role, makes a transcript and scores your answers for that listing. Most interviews take about 20 minutes, and you only need to finish each one once.

There is no human alternative. Mercor's docs say the AI interview is the only screening method, and it cannot be done by chat, phone call or any other format. Mercor's engineering blog names the interviewer Monty and says it runs around 10,000 conversations a day, about fifteen minutes each on average, across hundreds of job categories.
What the Mercor AI interview asks you

According to Mercor, the interviewer builds its questions from your resume and the job description, then transcribes and evaluates what you say. Some interviews are technical, others test language or reasoning. The blog post adds that the most common one, a general Domain Expert interview, makes up more than 70% of sessions, and that coding problems are generated from your profile.

If you pass an interview, the result carries over. Mercor calls this assessment reuse: a passed assessment does not need to be taken again for comparable roles, and a finished interview is kept when another application asks for the same one.
Before you start: setup that actually matters

paragraphs.title: 1. Do the free practice interview
paragraphs.text: Mercor offers a Practice Interview that is not tied to any application, does not affect your chances and can be repeated as often as you like. Practice interviews are not shared with companies, so use one to get used to the format.

paragraphs.title: 2. Use Chrome on a computer
paragraphs.text: Mercor recommends the latest Google Chrome. Edge and Safari are supported, Firefox is not. Some interviews need a computer; on a phone you will see a message saying the interview needs one, with a button to copy the link and open it on a laptop.

paragraphs.title: 3. Pass the setup checks
paragraphs.text: In the waiting room, the Setup checks tab tests your devices. Working mic is required, and so is screen sharing when the interview asks for it (share your entire screen, not one tab). Face in frame, good lighting, a working camera and a steady camera are not required, but Mercor says you need them for a clear recording. If Start interview stays gray, one required check has failed.

paragraphs.title: 4. Pick a quiet room
paragraphs.text: Mercor suggests a quiet space, a stable connection, headphones and an external mic. Keep your whole face visible. Interviews are in English unless the listing says otherwise. Pen and paper help, plus a calculator for number heavy roles.
During the interview
Speak clearly and keep answers tight. Mercor warns that long silences can make the AI jump in. If it interrupts you while you are thinking, the docs say you can simply tell it you were not finished.

Captions are on by default and can be turned off. Some interviews include a whiteboard that saves on its own. If something breaks, use the Help button inside the interview. If the bot stops answering, Mercor's checklist is to wait 30 to 60 seconds, refresh and rejoin, clear Chrome's cached files and cookies, and turn off VPNs, ad blockers and privacy extensions.

On AI help, the rules are strict. Mercor's LLM usage policy, as summarized in its interview FAQ, allows grammar and wording checks but bans using large language models to write your answers, rate model responses, write explanations or review code. The docs also ask candidates not to share specific questions or screenshots of the interview.
Retakes: you get three

You can retake an interview up to three times across all applications that use it. Open the Assessments tab, click Retake assessment on the interview card, pick a reason (the options include Technical issue, Interrupted and Improve performance) and click Retake interview. Only your most recent attempt is evaluated, and retaking resets your application progress.

Save retakes for real problems. Mercor's own waiting room note says hiring managers can see how many times you retook an interview. An attempt that ends far too early is marked Interview too short and does not count, but retaking it still uses one of your three.
After you submit

Your application shows Ready to submit or Submitted for each step. Mercor gives no timeline for results; you are told when the application moves to the next stage, and you can keep applying elsewhere. Mercor says it cannot give specific feedback on rejections because of volume, and a submitted application cannot be edited or withdrawn.

On data, Mercor keeps the video, audio and transcript of official interviews to judge your candidacy and recommend you to employers, and says it does not sell interview data. Its FAQ says interview data will not be used to train AI models; its data policy says the data does train Mercor's internal recommendation models but never third party language models. You cannot download your recording or transcript. You can delete your account and its data in Account Settings, unless you have an active contract, a payout in progress or an open offer.

The honest read: there is no trick to beat the Mercor AI interview. The interviewer works from your resume, so the best preparation is a clean, text based PDF resume that states your real experience, one practice run, and a setup that passes every check. Mercor's own resume rules ask for a PDF under 2 MB, one or two pages, with no images or tables.
